transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. If it's a gas oven, then no: the flame-failure device is part of the gas safety system, and in the UK any work on it should be done by a Gas Safe registered engineer. Please don't try to bypass it or keep the oven running by holding the knob in. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the flame-failure safety device. Is it a gas oven, and does the burner light at all or not even spark?
Yes, it's a gas oven. It lights fine and stays lit while I hold the knob in, it just goes out a few seconds after I let go. I also have a CO alarm in the kitchen and it hasn't sounded.
Could you tell me a bit more about what it is doing, and when it happens?

It started about a week ago. At first I just had to hold the knob in a bit longer, but now it won't stay lit even after 20-30 seconds. The hob burners and grill are fine. Only smell gas briefly while I'm trying to light it, which clears quickly.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.
